1.title: Tap, Tap, Drum!
1.topic: family music time with a drum, humming and clapping (family, music, play)
lines: *Tap*, | *tap*, | *tap* the *drum*.
*Dad* can *hum*. | *Hum*, | *hum*, | *hum*.
*Mom* can *clap*. | *Clap*, | *clap*, | *clap*.
The *cat* | *naps* on my *lap*.
*Bam*! | *Bam*! | It is *so* much *fun*! ↘
Come and *tap* with us, | *everyone*! ↘
sounds: tap, dad, clap, cat, nap, lap
입을 옆으로 크게 벌리고 '애'에 가깝게 짧게 말해요.
u는 힘을 빼고 짧게 '어'. drum은 '드럼'이 아니라 '드뤔'처럼 한 박자로 붙여요.
drum – hum, clap – lap, fun – everyone
끝소리가 같은 단어는 같은 박자로 또박또박, 리듬을 살려요.
1.expression: Tap the table on every “tap,” hum with closed lips, clap three times, whisper “The cat naps on my lap,” then shout “Bam! Bam!” and wave everyone in on the last line.

2.title: The Tulip Bulb
2.topic: planting a tulip bulb in fall and waiting all winter for it to bloom in spring (seasons, plants, patience)
lines: In *November*, | Lucy and Mom *planted* | a *tulip* bulb.
Lucy *patted* the dirt | and *watered* it.
The next *morning*, | she *rushed* outside. | “Is my *flower* up?” ↗
Mom *smiled*. | “It needs to *sleep* | all *winter*.”
Lucy *waited* | and *waited*. | Snow *covered* the ground.
Then one *spring* day, | she *spotted* | a little green *tip*.
It *grew* and *grew* | into a bright red *tulip*!
“It was *worth* the wait!” | Lucy *shouted*. ↘
sounds: t, d 뒤의 -ed는 '이드'로 한 박자 더: plant-ed '플랜티드'.
r, l, r 소리 뒤의 -ed는 짧은 d: smiled '스마일드'.
sh 뒤의 -ed는 t 소리: rushed '러쉬트'. '러쉬드'가 아니에요.
2.expression: Sound gentle while planting, hurry and hope on “Is my flower up?”, use Mom's calm voice, stretch out “waited and waited,” then sound surprised at the green tip and burst with joy on “It was worth the wait!”

3.title: How Bats See with Sound
3.topic: how bats use echolocation to find their way and catch insects at night (animals, science)
lines: Most *bats* fly at *night*, | when it is *dark* outside.
So *how* do they find their *way*? ↘ | They use their *ears*!
As a bat *flies*, | it makes *high*, | *squeaky* sounds.
The sounds are so *high* | that people *cannot* hear them.
The sounds *bounce* off trees, | walls, | and bugs, | and come back as *echoes*.
The bat *listens* to the echoes | to learn what is *nearby*.
If an echo comes back *fast*, | something is *close*.
If it takes *longer*, | the thing is *farther* away.
This special skill | is called *echolocation*.
With it, | one little bat can catch | *hundreds* of *insects* | in just *one* hour! ↘
sounds: 긴 단어는 힘주는 음절 하나만 크고 길게: echolocation은 'CA'에 힘!
서로 반대되는 말(fast/longer, close/farther)에 힘을 주면 뜻이 또렷해져요.
So how do they find their way? ↘
how, what, where 질문은 끝을 내려요. 대답 'They use their ears!'는 신나게.
3.expression: Read it like a nature-show host: a little mysterious on the dark night, curious on the question, excited on “They use their ears!”, clear and careful when you explain fast and slow echoes, and amazed on the last line.

4.title: The Thankful Chain
4.topic: a boy who can't think of what to be thankful for notices small kindnesses during Thanksgiving week and fills a paper chain (holidays, school, feelings, gratitude)
lines: The week before *Thanksgiving*, | Ms. Ortiz handed out | strips of *colorful* paper.
“Write one thing you're *thankful* for | on each strip,” | she *explained*. | “We'll link them into a *chain*.”
Leo stared at his *blank* strip | and *chewed* on his pencil.
He wrote “my dog, *Biscuit*,” | and then he got *stuck*.
“I can't think of *anything* else,” | he *sighed*. ↘
“Try *looking* around you today,” | Ms. Ortiz said *gently*. | “Thankful things are often *small*.”
At *recess*, | Leo *tripped* on the field, | and his friend Ana | helped him *up*.
At *lunch*, | the cafeteria worker | *remembered* that he liked | *extra* apple slices.
In the *afternoon*, | the heater *rattled* and stopped, | and Mr. Reyes, the *custodian*, | came to fix it *right* away.
On the bus ride *home*, | Leo pulled out *four* new strips | and began to *write*.
By *Friday*, | his strips *stretched* | from his desk | all the way to the *door*.
When the class hung the chain | across the *ceiling*, | it *looped* around the room | *three* times.
Leo *smiled* up | at all the *colors*. ↘
Ms. Ortiz was *right*: | thankful things *are* small, | but when you *add* them up, | they fill a *whole* room. ↘
sounds: At recess, | Leo tripped on the field, | and his friend Ana | helped him up.
| 마다 짧게 쉬고, 한 덩어리는 한 숨에 이어서 읽어요.
p, ch 뒤의 -ed는 t로 짧게: stretched '스트레치트'.
평소엔 약한 are에 힘을 주면 '정말 그렇다'는 뜻이 돼요.
4.expression: Read it like a warm storyteller: stuck and a little grumpy for Leo at first, kind and calm for Ms. Ortiz, quicker and brighter as Leo notices each small kindness, and slow and proud on the final line.
